firstMessage:
`checkRefundLimit` now throws the new `InvalidRefundAmountError` for a refund of zero or less, instead of `RefundTooLargeError`. The full suite passes: 37 tests, up from 36 because I added one.

Changes:
- **`src/refunds.ts`**: added and exported `InvalidRefundAmountError`, which follows the same pattern as the other error classes there. The zero-or-negative check now runs first and throws it. A positive amount above what is left on the charge still throws `RefundTooLargeError`.
- **`src/refunds.test.ts`**: the existing test expected zero to throw `RefundTooLargeError`, so I moved the zero case into a new test that expects `InvalidRefundAmountError` and also covers a negative amount.

Nothing else in the repo referenced the old behaviour. `R-REFUND-LIMIT` in `REQUIREMENTS.md` doesn't name an error class, so I left it alone. I didn't commit anything.
finalMessage:
I committed the change as `a33b37b` on a new branch, `refund-invalid-amount`, since `main` was the checked-out branch. The full suite passes (37 tests) after the commit.

The commit contains only `src/refunds.ts` and `src/refunds.test.ts`, with the Co-Authored-By line. I haven't pushed the branch or opened a PR; say if you want either.
